scenarios.description: A statically imported vulnerable binding is used directly in dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

evidence.rationale: The marked binding occurs directly inside the value expression of the inner-html sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML through a local variable.

evidence.rationale: The rendered variable is assigned from marked(input) and then passed to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output crosses a React prop boundary before reaching dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

evidence.rationale: The parent passes rendered as the html prop and HtmlView uses that prop in the sink.

scenarios.description: A CommonJS binding is passed directly to eval.

evidence.rationale: The require binding is used directly inside the eval argument.

scenarios.description: The vulnerable dependency is imported but never referenced by a component.

evidence.rationale: No reference to the marked binding exists inside the component.

scenarios.description: The dependency is used by a component that contains no registered security sink.

evidence.rationale: The output is rendered as a normal JSX text child and no configured sink is present.

scenarios.description: The component has a sink, but it receives a value unrelated to the dependency output.

evidence.rationale: marked(input) reaches only the pre element; the inner-html sink receives trustedHtml.

scenarios.description: A dynamic import is invoked without capturing the returned module binding.

evidence.rationale: The import promise is not assigned, so no local binding can be propagated to a sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output initialises React state and the state value reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

evidence.rationale: The useState initial value derives from marked(input), and html is passed to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches React state through its setter before the state reaches a sink.

evidence.rationale: setHtml receives marked(input), making the html state value tainted before it reaches the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output is propagated through useMemo into dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

evidence.rationale: The memoised html value is derived from marked(input) and is then passed to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output crosses a prop boundary into a sink component declared in another file.

evidence.rationale: CrossFileParent passes marked output as html; HtmlSink receives that prop and uses it in the sink.

scenarios.description: The vulnerable binding is used directly in a dynamic anchor href sink.

evidence.rationale: marked(input) occurs directly in the expression assigned to the anchor href sink.

scenarios.description: The vulnerable binding is assigned directly to innerHTML through a React ref.

evidence.rationale: marked(input) is the right-hand side of the ref.current.innerHTML assignment.

scenarios.description: A nested parameter shadows the vulnerable import at an eval sink.

evidence.rationale: The eval argument resolves to the nested marked parameter, not to the vulnerable imported binding.

scenarios.description: A location sink receives trusted input while dependency output is rendered separately.

evidence.rationale: The location assignment uses trustedUrl, while marked output only reaches the pre element.

scenarios.description: A bare CommonJS require loads the vulnerable package without capturing a binding.

evidence.rationale: The return value of require("marked") is not assigned to any local identifier.

scenarios.description: A JSX URL sink receives trusted input while dependency output is rendered separately.

evidence.rationale: The href expression references trustedUrl, while the marked-derived value reaches only pre.

scenarios.description: Relative import resolution selects a safe child despite a dangerous same-named component elsewhere.

evidence.rationale: SafeParent explicitly imports the safe Target; the unrelated same-named dangerous Target must not create an edge.

scenarios.description: A React class component uses dependency output only in a normal JSX text position.

evidence.rationale: The class render method uses marked output as a JSX text child and contains no configured sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output is used as the initial React reducer state and reaches a sink.

evidence.rationale: The useReducer initial state derives from marked(input), and the resulting html state reaches the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output propagates through a memoised callback and a local value into a sink.

evidence.rationale: makeHtml closes over marked(input); its return value is assigned to html and then reaches the sink.

scenarios.description: The vulnerable binding is passed directly to the global Function constructor.

evidence.rationale: marked(input) occurs directly in the final argument of the global Function constructor.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches insertAdjacentHTML through a local variable.

evidence.rationale: html derives from marked(input) and is passed as the content argument of insertAdjacentHTML.

scenarios.description: Dependency output crosses two component prop boundaries before reaching a sink.

evidence.rationale: MultiHopPropagation passes rendered to IntermediateComponent, which forwards it to FinalHtmlSink.

scenarios.description: A reducer supplies trusted data to a sink while dependency output is rendered separately.

evidence.rationale: safeHtml derives from trustedHtml; the marked-derived rendered value reaches only the pre element.

scenarios.description: A locally bound eval identifier must not be treated as the global eval sink.

evidence.rationale: eval resolves to the local safeEval binding, so the component contains no registered global eval sink.

scenarios.description: insertAdjacentHTML receives trusted data while dependency output is rendered separately.

evidence.rationale: The sink receives trustedHtml, while marked(input) is assigned to rendered and used only as JSX text.

scenarios.description: A destructured CommonJS binding is used in a component without a security sink.

evidence.rationale: The parse binding derives from require("marked") but its output is used only as a JSX text child.

scenarios.description: Dependency output crosses two prop boundaries but terminates in a normal JSX text position.

evidence.rationale: The value is forwarded through SafeIntermediate to SafeTerminal, which contains no registered sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches a sink through a custom hook-like function.

evidence.rationale: useRenderedMarkdown returns marked(input); CustomHookFlow assigns that return value to html and passes it to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches a component sink through a helper function imported from another file.

evidence.rationale: renderMarkdown returns marked(input); HelperFunctionFlow imports it, receives the returned html and passes it to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output crosses from a context provider to a consumer sink.

evidence.rationale: ContextProvider stores marked output in the provider value; ContextConsumer reads that value and passes it to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches a sink after assignment to an object member.

evidence.rationale: payload.html is assigned marked(input), and the same member is subsequently passed to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches a sink through array mutation and indexed retrieval.

evidence.rationale: marked(input) is pushed into values; values[0] is assigned to html and then passed to the sink.

scenarios.description: Dependency output reaches state and a sink from inside a Promise callback.

evidence.rationale: The Promise callback passes marked(value) to setHtml, and the corresponding html state is used in the sink.

scenarios.description: A tainted local binding is overwritten with trusted data before reaching the sink.

evidence.rationale: Although html initially receives marked output, the unconditional trustedHtml assignment is the last write before the sink.

scenarios.description: A child receives one tainted prop but its sink reads a distinct trusted prop through the generic props object.

evidence.rationale: unsafe carries marked output, but the child sink reads only props.trustedHtml; the properties are distinct.

scenarios.description: A rest-props object contains both tainted and trusted properties, while the sink reads only the trusted property.

evidence.rationale: rest.unsafe carries marked output, but the sink specifically reads rest.trustedHtml.

scenarios.description: An object contains a tainted property and a separate trusted property used by the sink.

evidence.rationale: payload.unsafe contains marked output, whereas the sink reads only payload.safe, which contains trustedHtml.

scenarios.description: Only the trusted property is destructured from an object that also contains a tainted property.

evidence.rationale: safe is destructured from payload.safe, which is trustedHtml; payload.unsafe is the only marked-derived property.

scenarios.description: An array contains tainted and trusted entries, while the sink reads only the trusted index.

evidence.rationale: values[0] contains marked output, but the sink reads values[1], which contains only trustedHtml.

scenarios.description: DOMPurify output is used directly by a React inner-HTML sink.

evidence.rationale: The vulnerable sanitizer binding is called inside the value supplied directly to dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

scenarios.description: DOMPurify output reaches a DOM innerHTML assignment through a local binding.

evidence.rationale: sanitizeHtml returns DOMPurify output; DompurifyLocalDomHtml imports the service and assigns its result to contentRef.current.innerHTML.

scenarios.description: DOMPurify output crosses a component props boundary before reaching an inner-HTML sink.

evidence.rationale: The sanitizer service feeds a custom hook; ArticlePage passes the hook result to ArticleContent, which consumes it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

scenarios.description: DOMPurify is imported but never referenced.

evidence.rationale: No reference to the imported DOMPurify binding exists in the source file.

scenarios.description: A DOMPurify-derived local is unconditionally overwritten before the sink.

evidence.rationale: The last write to html calls a policy function that returns reviewed static content, so the dependency output has no demonstrated path to the sink.

scenarios.description: A DOMPurify-derived object property is separate from the reviewed property consumed by the sink.

evidence.rationale: The service stores DOMPurify output in payload.dependencyOutput, whereas the page forwards only payload.reviewedHtml from the policy module to ArticleContent.

scenarios.description: serialize-javascript output is embedded directly in the contents of a script element.

evidence.rationale: The vulnerable serializer call occurs inside the template literal passed directly to dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

scenarios.description: serialize-javascript output reaches insertAdjacentHTML through a local script body.

evidence.rationale: The state loader feeds the serializer service through a custom hook; the page interpolates the resulting scriptBody into insertAdjacentHTML.

scenarios.description: serialize-javascript output reaches a component sink through an imported helper function.

evidence.rationale: The app-shell path normalizes state, serializes it in a dedicated service, builds a bootstrap script and supplies that result to dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

scenarios.description: serialize-javascript is used in a component that has no registered sink.

evidence.rationale: The page passes serialized state to a presentation component that renders only a normal JSX text child; neither component has a configured sink.

scenarios.description: The component contains serializer output and a separate sink that consumes only reviewed content.

evidence.rationale: Serialized state reaches only StatePreview; the script sink receives an independent value returned by the reviewed-bootstrap policy.

scenarios.description: serialize-javascript is dynamically imported without capturing a module binding.

evidence.rationale: The dynamic import promise is not captured, so no dependency binding can reach a sink.
